sources.entry: iTunes-Volume-Control - This app allows you to control the iTunes volume using volume up and volume down hotkeys.

summary.one_liner: A discontinued macOS menu-bar app that maps keyboard volume keys and Apple Remote buttons to the volume of Apple Music/iTunes and Spotify, rather than the system volume.
summary.what_it_does: The app intercepts the keyboard volume-up and volume-down keys and applies them to the volume of Apple Music or Spotify, instead of only the global system volume. It also lets the Apple Remote change the same player volume, which matters for AirPlay devices whose level follows the player's volume. If neither player is playing, the keys fall back to the global volume. Holding the command key switches between controlling the system volume and the player volume. Users can adjust the volume step size and turn off the on-screen volume overlay. The README describes a mute control and an option to hide the status bar icon, and notes that the overlay uses the native macOS HUD.
use_cases: control Apple Music volume from the keyboard
adjust Spotify volume with volume keys
change AirPlay device volume on a Mac
use an Apple Remote to set music volume
hide the volume overlay while watching movies
how_to_run: Download the zip file from the project's releases
Drag the app into the Applications folder or another folder
Run the app; a music note icon appears in the status bar
Authorize it in Security & Privacy and Accessibility settings when prompted
Grant access to Music and Spotify when the dialog appears
notable: Controls the volume of the music player itself (Apple Music, Spotify) rather than only the system volume, which affects AirPlay output levels
Command key toggles between system volume and player volume
Apple Remote support, adapted from iremotepipe
Uses the native macOS heads-up display for the volume overlay, with an option to hide it
Successor app 'Volume Control' is notarised by Apple; this repository is archival
caveats: No longer maintained; the repository is kept for archival purposes only
The README points users to the successor app, Volume Control, which replaces it
Requires macOS accessibility and AppleEvents permissions to be granted manually
The README's requirements list macOS Mojave or Catalina, and a later section mentions OS X 10.7 (Lion), which is inconsistent with the rest of the document
